title: How can twelve squared help us square other numbers?
description: The book says twelve squared is one hundred forty four and asks for the squares of one point two, zero point one two, zero point zero one two and one hundred twenty. Each number is twelve divided or multiplied by a power of ten, and the square changes by that power twice.
teaching_notes: One idea: when a number is changed by a power of ten, its square is changed by that power twice. Watch for students who move the point only once in the square.

video_script.why: Each number is twelve moved by a power of ten, so its square is 144 moved by that power twice.
video_script.substitution: Write each number as twelve divided or multiplied by a power of ten, then square both parts.
video_script.anchor: twelve squared is 144, and four numbers made from twelve
video_script.payoff_line: A change by ten in the number is a change by a hundred in the square

final_answer.spoken: One point two squared is one point four four. Zero point one two squared is zero point zero one four four. Zero point zero one two squared is zero point zero zero zero one four four. One hundred twenty squared is fourteen thousand four hundred.

maths_rules: check by places: 1, 2, 3 decimal places give 2, 4, 6 places in the squares
video_script.design: Twelve squared stays in a card at the left. Each of the four numbers is shown as twelve divided or multiplied by a power of ten, with its square beside it.

<bookmark mark='more'/>Also zero point zero one two squared, and one hundred twenty squared.
How can twelve squared help us find all four?

<bookmark mark='sq4'/>Its square is one hundred forty four times one hundred.

<bookmark mark='ans2'/>Zero point zero one two squared is zero point zero zero zero one four four.
One hundred twenty squared is fourteen thousand four hundred.
